studies.title: An Excellent Pattern To Follow
studies.meaning: The word rendered as example means a model that is copied, and the sentence attaches a condition to it. It is an excellent pattern for whoever hopes for God and the last day and remembers God often, so what a person is looking for determines whether the pattern is available to them at all. The second ayah then shows the thing in operation. Facing an army assembled to finish them, the believers identified it as what they had been told to expect, and the recognition raised their confidence rather than lowering it.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, from the siege in which allied clans marched on Medina. A ditch was dug across the exposed northern approach and held for weeks in cold weather with rations short and families moved into fortified quarters. The surah gives its opening section to that episode, and these two ayat sit deliberately between a description of those who found reasons to withdraw and a description of those who kept their word.

keyTerms.note: Something one takes as a template for one's own conduct, from a root connected with setting a thing right by matching it to another. It implies imitation in practice, not admiration at a distance.
The plural of a party or faction bound together for a purpose. It names an alliance of clans that would ordinarily be rivals, which is what made the sight of them outside the town so alarming.
From the root of peace and of handing something over intact. Paired with faith, it names the settling of the matter rather than the belief itself, the point where argument stops.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Arabian warfare was raiding: a fast approach, a fight, a withdrawal within a day. A coalition camped outside a town for weeks was outside everyone's experience, which is part of why the ditch was dug at all. Men worked in shifts turning earth in the cold with rations short enough that the accounts remember what people did and did not eat during it.
studies.didYouKnow: The surah takes its name from that coalition, and the campaign carries two names in the tradition: one after the confederated clans who came, and one after the ditch that was dug against them. The same weeks are therefore remembered both by who arrived and by what was built, depending on which account is being told.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Setting a person rather than a rule as the model changes what following means. A rule can be satisfied exactly and then set down; a pattern has to be read into circumstances it never met, which requires the attention the same ayah calls frequent remembrance. The second ayah adds something about belief itself: it grew at the moment the danger was confirmed, so what strengthened them was accuracy rather than reassurance.

crossReferences.why: Uses the identical word of Abraham and those with him, showing the pattern is not unique to one messenger.
States what is being copied in one line, that he stands upon a great and settled character.
Gives the narrative of the same siege, including the wind and the hosts that were sent against it.

studies.applyIt: Think of one person whose steadiness under pressure you have actually watched, not read about. Identify a single small thing they do, the pause before answering, the way they eat properly on a bad day, and copy that one thing this week. A pattern is only followed in details; admiring the whole of it costs nothing and changes nothing.

studies.title: Men True To Their Pledge
studies.meaning: A short ayah about keeping a word. The men described made an undertaking to God and matched it, and they are then sorted into two groups: those who have completed what they took on and those still waiting to. Scholars differ over the word for what was completed, reading it as a vow discharged, as a life run to its term, or as death met in the manner promised, and the commentaries record the range rather than settling it. The last clause states the whole matter negatively: they changed nothing at all.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, from the weeks of the siege of Medina. The classical sources connect the ayah with men who had given an undertaking before an earlier engagement and then held to it, and their reports name several individuals and differ over which is meant. What the accounts agree on is the shape of the situation: a pledge given while nothing was happening, and kept once the danger arrived and the reasons for withdrawing had become obvious.

keyTerms.note: A mutual undertaking, from a root meaning to keep something in view and return to it. The word implies an obligation a person is expected to revisit rather than one discharged and forgotten.
A word that occurs only here in the whole Quran, which is why the commentaries record several readings of it: a vow paid, a lifespan completed, or a death accepted in advance.
To put one thing in the place of another. Denying it twice over, with a noun repeating the verb, is a construction of emphasis: not the smallest substitution was made.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: An oath in Arabia was public and physical, given by clasping hands in front of witnesses, and it bound a man's whole standing. Someone who broke one was satirised in verse and the verse outlived him. In fighting, a man who had sworn to hold a position and then left it was disgraced permanently, and the memory of it attached to his sons, so the cost of a broken pledge was measured in generations.
studies.didYouKnow: The word translated as vow in this ayah appears nowhere else in the Quran. A single occurrence gives the philologists very little to work from, which is exactly why the classical commentaries preserve three readings of it side by side rather than choosing, and why translations of this line differ from one another more than usual.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Truthfulness is presented as a match between a sentence and a later life rather than as accuracy in reporting facts. The division into those who have finished and those still waiting is the striking part: the ones who have not yet been tested are counted among the truthful already, so the category is defined by an intention that has not moved rather than by an outcome that can be checked.

crossReferences.why: Describes a pledge given by hand and states plainly what fulfilling it is answered with.
Includes keeping a covenant once made in its short list of what actually counts as righteousness.
Puts the same undertaking as a transaction and asks who is more faithful to a covenant than God.

studies.applyIt: Find one promise you made that has quietly gone unmentioned for months. This week either do it, or tell the person plainly that you will not and why. The ayah's final phrase is about not substituting anything, and a promise silently replaced by nothing is the substitution that is easiest to make and hardest to notice.

studies.title: Ten Qualities Named Twice
studies.meaning: Ten qualities are listed, and each is named twice over, once in the masculine and once in the feminine, with no difference in the description and one reward announced at the end for the whole set. The list runs from submission and belief through devotion, truthfulness, patience, humility, giving, fasting, restraint and remembrance. Only the last carries a qualifier, and it is about frequency rather than about degree. Read aloud, the doubling is the most audible feature of the ayah.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The classical commentators report an occasion for this ayah on which the sources broadly agree: women of the community asked why the revelation addressed men in its wording and did not mention them, and this ayah followed. The reports differ over which woman put the question and in what setting, but the substance of the account is consistent across them and is given by the major commentaries.

keyTerms.note: From a root meaning to stand in sustained obedience, and used of long standing in prayer. The word carries steadiness over time rather than compliance in a single instance.
Used of ground that has sunk and of a voice dropping. It describes a lowering that happens in the presence of something, not a modest opinion a person holds about themselves.
The only quality in the list given a qualifier, and the qualifier is frequency rather than intensity. It covers both calling to mind and saying aloud, with no line drawn between them.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Women in Medina farmed, traded, held property in their own names and treated the wounded after engagements. Public religious life in Arabia, though, had been male in its forms: the custodians of the sanctuary, the poets who spoke for a tribe, the men who settled disputes in assembly. An address that named both sides in identical terms, ten times in succession, was formally unusual in that setting.
studies.didYouKnow: This is the Quran's most sustained use of paired masculine and feminine forms. The ayah is a single sentence in which each masculine plural is immediately followed by its feminine counterpart, ten times, before the sentence finally reaches its verb and states one reward for all twenty groups at once.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The list is of qualities rather than of roles, and the reward is stated once for the whole of it, which places the same standard on everyone named. It also amounts to a compact account of what the Quran counts as religious life, and the balance is worth noticing: most items are interior states or habits, and only two of the ten would be visible to somebody watching from outside.

crossReferences.why: States the same equality as a principle: no worker's work is lost, male or female, each from the other.
Attaches a good life in this world to the same condition, whoever does good and believes, male or female.
Applies it to the outcome, entry to the Garden granted on the same terms without the smallest reduction.

studies.applyIt: Read the ten qualities slowly and pick the one you would score lowest on, honestly rather than modestly. Then do the smallest possible version of it today: one honest sentence, one held tongue, one thing given away. Ten is a long list, and the point of a long list is that nobody is expected to start at the top of it.

studies.title: The Seal Of The Prophets
studies.meaning: A denial and a title arrive in one sentence: he is not the father of any of your men, and he is the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets. Commentators read the seal in two connected senses that are both early, the stamp that closes a document and the last item in a sequence, and they generally hold them together rather than choosing. What follows is unexpected. After a statement of that weight, the address turns to the believers and asks for remembrance, frequent, morning and evening.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The ayah follows a passage concerning the household of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Arabian custom by which an adopted son took his father's name and stood in a son's place for inheritance and marriage. The surah has already stated that lineage would not be reckoned that way. The denial at the opening of this ayah belongs to that discussion before it turns into a statement about prophecy.

keyTerms.note: The signet pressed into clay to shut a letter. A seal both ends a document and certifies it, which is why the word carries finality and confirmation together rather than one at the expense of the other.
The verbal noun placed after its own verb for emphasis, so the instruction reads as remembering with real remembrance. The added word for abundance then makes frequency part of the request.
The stretch between the sun losing its heat and dusk, not night. Paired with early morning it marks the two ends of the working day rather than the hours when nothing else is happening.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A seal was ordinary equipment for anyone who sent letters: a ring pressed into soft clay closed the roll and told the recipient who had sent it, and it was the last thing applied before dispatch. Adoption in Arabia transferred name, inheritance and standing. Saying of a man that he was father to none of the men present was therefore a heavy social statement before it was anything else.
studies.didYouKnow: The Prophet's personal name appears only four times in the whole Quran, and this is one of them. Everywhere else he is addressed or described by title: messenger, prophet, the one wrapped in a cloak, the one addressed as you. The name itself is reserved for a handful of statements about who he is and is not.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Two claims are made together: that the line of prophecy is complete, and that what closes it also authenticates what came before. The instruction that follows is the surprising half. Immediately after a statement about revelation ending, what the community is asked for is not a doctrine to defend but a practice to keep twice daily, which places the continuity in remembrance rather than in any line of succession.

crossReferences.why: Uses the name in the same way, to fix that he is a messenger and that messengers have passed before.
States the scope this ayah implies, a message addressed to all people rather than to one community.
Gives the same two-ended instruction about remembering the name of your Lord, morning and evening.

studies.applyIt: Pick one fixed point in your morning and one in your evening, the kettle boiling or the front door closing, and attach a short phrase of remembrance to each. Keep both under ten seconds. The ayah asks for frequency rather than length, and frequency is built on things that were going to happen anyway.

studies.title: God And His Angels Do This
studies.meaning: Something is stated before anything is asked. God and His angels do this, and only then are the believers told to join in. The commentators note that the single verb carries a different sense for each subject: from God it is mercy and honour extended, from the angels it is the asking for that, and from human beings it is a request made. So one word covers three actions, and what the community is invited into is already under way rather than being started by them.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The surah has been setting out how people should conduct themselves around the Prophet's household, down to waiting for an invitation before entering and leaving once a meal is finished. This ayah sits inside that stretch and lifts the subject from courtesy at a doorway to a formula of honour. The sources report that the companions asked how the words should be said, and preserve accounts of the reply.

keyTerms.note: The verb behind the word for prayer, whose root sense is to incline toward or attend to. That one root can serve God, angels and people is why the classical explanation gives it three senses here.
From the root of soundness and safety. The greeting it names is a declaration that the other person is secure from you, which is why it doubles as the ordinary word for making peace.
The verbal noun repeating its own verb, a construction of emphasis. It asks for the greeting given properly and completely rather than muttered as a reflex in passing.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Forms of address were formal and public in Arabia. How a man was greeted on entering a gathering announced his standing, and poets were paid to compose praise for patrons that would be repeated at assemblies for years afterwards. A community that saw its messenger daily, sat with him and ate in his house, was here given a settled formula of honour for a person who was also a neighbour.
studies.didYouKnow: The same verb returns thirteen ayat later, at forty-three, where God and His angels are said to do this for the believers themselves, bringing them out of darkness into light. Within one surah the action moves in both directions: the community is asked to offer it toward the Prophet, and is told it is already being offered toward them.
studies.theologicalSignificance: People are invited to take part in something described as already happening, which is an unusual structure for an instruction. It is not a duty to be discharged but a joining. The passage also places honour toward the messenger inside worship rather than beside it, while keeping the direction of the request unambiguous: what is being asked for is asked from God, and the asking is what human beings contribute.

crossReferences.why: Turns the same verb toward the believers, with the stated purpose of bringing them out of darkness.
Uses the same language of blessings and mercy descending, here upon those who hold under loss.
Shows the human form of the verb in use, a prayer offered over people as a settling for them.

studies.applyIt: The next time his name comes up, in a talk or a conversation or your own reading, say the words slowly instead of running them together under your breath. Once, deliberately, with the meaning of each half in mind. The ayah asks for the greeting given fully, and most of us long ago stopped hearing what we are saying.

studies.title: Speak In A Straight Manner
studies.meaning: A warning drawn from an earlier community, then an instruction about speech. The believers are told not to be like those who caused hurt to Moses by what they said, and the text adds that God cleared him of it. The commentators record several accounts of what was said and do not settle on one, though they agree the injury was verbal and that it came from his own people. The instruction that follows names the alternative in a single word, used of an arrow that flies true and a wall built without a lean.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, near the end of a surah that has been dealing throughout with talk inside the community: rumour touching the Prophet's household, the excuses of those who withdrew during the siege, and speech that damaged people who had done nothing. These two ayat generalise from the specific incidents the surah has been addressing into a standard for speech that outlasts the occasions which produced it.

keyTerms.note: A verb for injury that stops short of physical harm: annoyance, insult, the wearing damage of being talked about. It is the word the Quran uses for what words do rather than what hands do.
From the word for a face. Someone of standing is one whose face is known and welcomed, so the vindication is described in exactly the currency that the slander had attacked.
Used of an arrow that flies true and of a wall built without a lean. It names accuracy and soundness together, so right speech is defined by hitting the mark rather than by being pleasant.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Reputation was the whole of a person's social capital, and it travelled by mouth through a town small enough for a story to cross it before noon. Satire was a recognised craft with paid practitioners, and a well-made line about a man could outlive him and follow his children. Nothing was written down to check a claim against, so a correction never travelled as fast as the original did.
studies.didYouKnow: Moses is named more often in the Quran than any other individual, well over a hundred times. Here he appears in none of the roles the name usually carries. He is not confronting Pharaoh, not receiving the tablets, not parting the sea. He is a man who was talked about unfairly by the people he had led, and who was cleared by someone other than himself.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The vindication is placed in God's hands: the text says God cleared him, not that he cleared himself. That has a consequence for anyone being spoken about, since it removes the obligation to win the argument. The instruction then turns to the other side of the exchange, the people doing the speaking, and the word it uses for right speech names accuracy and structural soundness rather than tact.

crossReferences.why: Sets out the same territory in detail: ridicule, nicknames, suspicion, and speaking about people behind them.
Records Moses asking his own people directly why they injure him when they know who sent him.
Describes a rumour moving through a community and the sentence that should have stopped it.

studies.applyIt: Recall the last thing you passed on about someone that you had no way of checking. You do not need to undo it. Just let the next one stop with you: hear it, say nothing, and do not repeat it to the one person you would normally tell. Notice how strong the pull to pass it on actually is.
